content:
Soojin Lee: Heads up: Applied ML says we have a new model release we *could* include. Question for today: do we patch the PDF/report (v1.1) or do an addendum blog + update the interactive table only?

Ethan Wallace: Which model + what changed? (new SKU in catalog vs existing model got a new serving profile?)

Jonas Weber: New model in catalog. Think “Model X v2” class. We have runs for 3 regions already, can sweep the rest by EOW if Fleet can reserve.

Claire Dubois: It’s meaningfully better on latency/$ in our harness. Not just noise. But we need to be careful: prompt set v3 stays the same; only model changes.

Ben Carter: From GTM POV: “new model drops, updated benchmark” is a nice reactivation angle. But patching PDF means re-review + re-export + re-upload. Addendum blog is faster.

Henry Cho: Product angle: interactive table should reflect current catalog, otherwise it’s stale a week after launch. I’m +1 update table regardless. PDF… less sure.

Wei Chen: Docs site: updating the interactive JSON feed is straightforward. Updating the PDF means changing the artifact + checks (links, sizes) + re-run the release pipeline.

Alicia Perez: Design: if PDF changes, all the ranking callouts/figure captions have to be re-checked. Risk we introduce inconsistency between charts + narrative.

Soojin Lee: Right. Legal also has feelings about “report updates” vs “new post.” @Michael @Sofia can you weigh in?

Michael Grant: If you materially change rankings/claims in the PDF, we treat it as a refreshed publication. That triggers the comparative-claims checklist again + new substantiation snapshot. Addendum blog can be framed as “additional data since publication,” with clear date + link to methodology.

Sofia Mendes: +1. Also we should avoid “v1.1” language that implies the original report had errors. Better: “Benchmark update (Month Day): added results for <model>.” Maintain a changelog.

Tyler Benson: Ops note: if we replace the PDF at the same URL, attribution gets messy (downloads vs version). Prefer keeping the original PDF stable and adding a new downloadable “update note” or addendum page.

Logan Wright: Analytics: interactive page updates are fine; we can version the dataset in the backend and emit an event like `benchmark_dataset_version_loaded` so we know what users saw.

Ethan Wallace: Content question: does the new model change any of the “top insight” bullets? If yes, addendum blog feels cleaner than stealth-editing the report copy.

Jonas Weber: It will likely take the #1 spot in 2 regions. The overall narrative (“production economics vary by region + workload; Redwood consistent across deployments”) still holds.

Claire Dubois: We should also note stability: we only have n=3 sweeps right now. For publication I’d want the standard stability gate pass + reruns on p95 variance.

Ben Carter: Timeline: if we wait for full sweeps + stability gates, we’re looking at next week for anything “official.” Blog addendum can ship once data’s validated.

Soojin Lee: Proposal: 1) Update interactive table when data validated. 2) Publish an addendum blog post (“New model added to the benchmark dataset”) with date + dataset version. 3) Keep PDF unchanged for now, but add a small note on landing page “dataset updated on X.” Thoughts?

Henry Cho: Works for me. Also, we should add a filter badge in table UI like “New” next to the model for a couple weeks.

Alicia Perez: UI badge is easy. Also add tooltip explaining “added on <date>, results based on methodology v1.”

Wei Chen: I can put a small callout on landing page under the table: “Dataset version: 2025-07-xx” and link to changelog.

Tyler Benson: Yes please on changelog. Keep it simple (date, what changed, any caveats).

Ethan Wallace: For addendum blog, I’ll draft ~600–900 words: why we added it, quick chart, how to interpret, link to methodology + JSON download.

Soojin Lee: Great. Jonas/Claire: can you confirm when stability gates will be green + provide the exact dataset version string we should reference?

Jonas Weber: If Fleet confirms capacity today, we can finish sweeps Thu, validation Fri AM. Dataset version string will be something like `2025-07-10-r2` (Mei has the convention).

Claire Dubois: I’ll also provide a short “what changed / what didn’t” paragraph for the addendum (prompt set same, concurrency same, caching policy same).

Michael Grant: Please route the addendum draft through Legal before it goes live. Watch the phrasing: avoid “fastest”/“best overall.” Prefer “in our benchmark harness” + “results may vary.”

Sofia Mendes: And if any graphics show competitor baselines, include the same caveats as the report. If it’s Redwood-only, simpler.

Ben Carter: Growth: we can do a re-engagement email “Benchmark dataset updated: new model added” to previous landing page visitors. Keep it factual.

Noura El-Khoury: Community: if we post on Hacker News / Reddit, we need a crisp line for “why no PDF update?” People will ask.

Soojin Lee: Suggested response: “PDF is a point-in-time report; interactive table + dataset are updated with versioning + changelog. We publish addenda for material additions.”

Logan Wright: Also note: we should pin the dataset version on the interactive page in the UI so screenshots have context. Saves us support headaches.

Wei Chen: +1. I’ll add “Dataset: YYYY-MM-DD (changelog)” right above the table.

Ethan Wallace: Question: do we call it “addendum” or “update”? “Addendum” feels formal; “Update” might read better.

Soojin Lee: Let’s call it “Benchmark Update: Added <model> results” (no implication we fixed anything). :thumbsup:

Jonas Weber: One more thing: if we publish before full APAC runs, we should say “currently available for NA/EU; APAC coming.” Otherwise people will read absence as poor performance.

Claire Dubois: Agree. We can also show a “data pending” state in table for missing regions.

Alicia Perez: I’ll mock the “pending” state text so it doesn’t look broken.

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- Jonas/Claire: confirm sweep schedule + stability gates ETA
- Ethan: draft update post (send to Soojin + Legal)
- Wei/Alicia: landing page + table UI dataset version + changelog link + “new” badge
- Logan/Tyler: dataset version instrumentation + reporting note
We’ll *not* patch the PDF this round.

Michael Grant: Works. When the update post is ready, tag me + Sofia. We’ll turn around quickly if claims stay scoped.

Ben Carter: I’ll prep the email variant but will wait for dataset version/date. Also can A/B subject lines.

Noura El-Khoury: I’ll draft the community response snippets + FAQ entry (“How often do you update?”) and send for review.

Soojin Lee: Thanks all. Please keep any external replies consistent: “interactive dataset is versioned + reproducible; report PDF is a snapshot.”
